questions.cardText:
[Zoology] What does the pajama shark’s egg look like?
A. It has tendrils
B. It is pitch black on one side and white on the other side
C. It has a pyramid shape
Answer: A. The egg cases of the pajama shark, also known as “mermaid’s purses,” have long, curly tendrils that help anchor them to seaweed and rocks, preventing them from drifting away in the ocean currents.
questions.de: Was hat die Eikapsel des Pyjamahais („Nixentäschchen“) an ihren Ecken, um sich an Algen und anderen Strukturen unter Wasser zu verankern?
questions.en: What does the pyjama shark's egg case (“mermaid's purse”) have at its corners to anchor it to seaweed and other underwater structures?

timeline.labelEn: Johann Friedrich Gmelin first describes the pyjama shark as Squalus africanus
timeline.labelDe: Johann Friedrich Gmelin beschreibt den Pyjamahai erstmals als Squalus africanus

questions.notes: Wikipedia: rectangular dark brown capsule ~9.5 cm long with long tendrils at the corners for fastening to algae stipes or gorgonians. Card correct.

questions.cardText:
[Linguistics] What does the word “Hallelujah” mean?
A. Praise the Lord
B. Rejoice with the Lord
C. Gratitude to the Lord
Answer: A. “Hallelujah” is derived from the Hebrew words “hallel,” meaning praise, and “Yah,” a shortened form of Yahweh, the name for God.
questions.de: Was bedeutet das hebräische Wort „Halleluja“ wörtlich?
questions.en: What does the Hebrew word “Hallelujah” literally mean?

timeline.labelEn: The Psalms, where 'Hallelujah' appears 24 times, are composed (10th to 5th century BC)
timeline.labelDe: Die Psalmen, in denen „Halleluja“ 24-mal vorkommt, entstehen (10. bis 5. Jahrhundert v. Chr.)

questions.notes: Wikipedia: hallelu = 'praise ye', Yah = short form of YHWH. Timeline from Wikipedia 'Psalms' (composition spans 10th century BCE to post-exilic, not earlier than 5th century BCE).
